description: End-to-end coverage of the `junit` and `markdown` reporters through the real CLI. A reporter only runs after every spec in its own run finishes, so a spec can never observe its own reporter output — each test seeds a tiny inner spec, spawns a nested `doc-detective` run with the reporter selected, and asserts on the file it wrote. Everything is shell-only (`node -e`), so no browser, driver or device is needed and every permutation runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. All scratch output lands in `.tmp/` at the repo root, never inside `test/core-artifacts/`: a stray `.doc-detective/` would break the fixture-bundle coverage test, and `.xml`/`.md` leftovers would be detected as documentation on later runs.

tests.description: `--reporters junit` with a directory output writes a parseable `junit.xml` containing a testcase per context.

runShell.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),{XMLParser}=require('fast-xml-parser');const x=fs.readFileSync('.tmp/fixture-reporters/junit-dir/out/junit.xml','utf8');const d=new XMLParser({ignoreAttributes:false,attributeNamePrefix:'@_'}).parse(x);const t=Number(d.testsuites['@_tests']);if(!(t>=1)){console.error('expected at least one testcase, got '+t);process.exit(1)}if(Number(d.testsuites['@_failures'])!==0){console.error('expected no failures');process.exit(1)}console.log('junit-dir ok, testcases: '+t)"

tests.description: `--reporters markdown` with a directory output writes `doc-detective-summary.md` with the summary table.

runShell.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const m=fs.readFileSync('.tmp/fixture-reporters/md-dir/out/doc-detective-summary.md','utf8');if(m.indexOf('# Doc Detective results')!==0){console.error('missing title');process.exit(1)}if(m.indexOf('| Steps |')<0){console.error('missing summary table');process.exit(1)}console.log('md-dir ok')"

tests.description: Both reporters together with an explicit `.xml` output: `junit` honors the exact path it was given, and `markdown` writes its fixed name beside it rather than treating the `.xml` path as a directory.

A failing inner run produces a `<failure>` element and a markdown summary naming the failing step. The inner run deliberately omits `--exit-on-fail`, so a FAILed inner test still exits 0 and this outer step passes.

runShell.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),{XMLParser}=require('fast-xml-parser');const b='.tmp/fixture-reporters/junit-fail/out/';const x=fs.readFileSync(b+'junit.xml','utf8');const d=new XMLParser({ignoreAttributes:false,attributeNamePrefix:'@_'}).parse(x);if(Number(d.testsuites['@_failures'])<1){console.error('expected a failure in junit.xml');process.exit(1)}if(x.indexOf('<failure')<0){console.error('expected a failure element');process.exit(1)}const m=fs.readFileSync(b+'doc-detective-summary.md','utf8');if(m.indexOf('## Failures')<0){console.error('expected a failures section');process.exit(1)}console.log('junit-fail ok')"

tests.description: A run that matches no tests still emits a parseable `<testsuites tests="0">` and a non-empty markdown summary. A zero-byte file is what a CI JUnit parser rejects, and a rejected file reads as 'no tests ran' rather than as an error.

runShell.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),{XMLParser}=require('fast-xml-parser');const b='.tmp/fixture-reporters/empty/out/';const x=fs.readFileSync(b+'junit.xml','utf8');if(x.length===0){console.error('junit.xml is empty');process.exit(1)}const d=new XMLParser({ignoreAttributes:false,attributeNamePrefix:'@_'}).parse(x);if(Number(d.testsuites['@_tests'])!==0){console.error('expected tests=0');process.exit(1)}const m=fs.readFileSync(b+'doc-detective-summary.md','utf8');if(m.trim().length===0){console.error('markdown summary is empty');process.exit(1)}console.log('empty-run ok')"
